chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Writing originals for Jimmy Dorsey and Dorsey's publishing company
summary: Horace wrote originals for Dorsey while the band had Bob Eberly and Helen O'Connell; bandleaders had publishing companies to profit from recorded originals.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Yeah. You also included Jimmy Dorsey here as -- when was this that you were writing for Jimmy Dorsey?

Well, I think that was in the '30's, early '30's, I think. I'm not too well up on that this morning with the times, so I (unintelligible) don't want to be misquoted. But I did a few things for him -- this was during the days when he had that great team of Bob Eberly and Helen OConnell.

but I did some original things for Jimmy. He liked those things, you know. He also had a publishing company. Seemed like in those days the guys wanted to do things for them that they could take over, and especially if they would record them. There was a royalty factor in that, plus the fact that -- well, they were business, you know.
Far more so than today, you know.

And I did some things with him. I didn't even name the tunes, you know, but I'd bring it, and I (unintelligible) and it would have a nice little beat to it. This is all he wanted -- and the big band sound, of course. And I remember, though, that I had made a couple of popular tunes for him, and I got the key for Eberly, one of the things, you know, (unintelligible) -- I'm trying to recall what the name was. I may get back to it, but this is the story on Jimmy.
